sanskrit: nyāyenopārjitāhārāḥ svakarmaniratā vayam vedāṃś ca brahmacaryeṇa nyāyataḥ prārthayāmahe
english: We win our food by lawful means, devoted to our own duties, and we seek to master the Vedas through chastity, in accordance with right law.

sanskrit: nyāyenottarakālaṃ ca gṛhebhyo niḥsṛtā vayam dharmadṛṣṭair vidhidvārais tapas tapsyāmahe vayam
english: And in due course, having lawfully gone forth from our homes, we shall practice austerity by the prescribed gateways that are sanctioned by righteousness.

sanskrit: bhavataḥ samyag eṣā hi buddhir hiṃsāvivarjitā etām ahiṃsāṃ yajñeṣu brūyās tvaṃ satataṃ prabho
english: This resolve of yours is wholly right, free from all violence; proclaim this non-injury at sacrifices forever, O lord.

sanskrit: prītās tato bhaviṣyāmo vayaṃ dvijavarottama visarjitāḥ samāptau ca satrād asmād vrajāmahe
english: Then we shall be well pleased, O best of the twice-born; and being released at the conclusion, we shall depart from this sacrificial session.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca tathā kathayatām eva devarājaḥ puraṃdaraḥ vavarṣa sumahātejā dṛṣṭvā tasya tapobalam
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Even as they were speaking thus, the king of the gods, Puraṃdara of mighty splendor, beholding the power of his austerity, sent down rain.

sanskrit: asamāptau ca yajñasya tasyāmitaparākramaḥ nikāmavarṣī devendro babhūva janamejaya
english: And before the sacrifice was concluded, O Janamejaya, Indra, lord of the gods, of measureless valor, became a rainer of showers at will.

sanskrit: prasādayām āsa ca tam agastyaṃ tridaśeśvaraḥ svayam abhyetya rājarṣe puraskṛtya bṛhaspatim
english: And the lord of the thirty gods himself came forth, O royal sage, and, placing Bṛhaspati before him, conciliated that Agastya.

sanskrit: tato yajñasamāptau tān visasarja mahāmunīn agastyaḥ paramaprītaḥ pūjayitvā yathāvidhi
english: Then, at the close of the sacrifice, Agastya, supremely pleased, honored those great sages according to rule and dismissed them.

sanskrit: janamejaya uvāca ko 'sau nakularūpeṇa śirasā kāñcanena vai prāha mānuṣavad vācam etat pṛṣṭo vadasva me
english: Janamejaya said: Who was that, in the form of a mongoose with a golden head, who spoke in a human voice? Tell me this, for I ask you.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca etat pūrvaṃ na pṛṣṭo 'haṃ na cāsmābhiḥ prabhāṣitam śrūyatāṃ nakulo yo 'sau yathā vāg asya mānuṣī
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Of this I was not asked before, nor was it told by us. Let it be heard who that mongoose was, and how his speech was human.

sanskrit: śrāddhaṃ saṃkalpayām āsa jamadagniḥ purā kila homadhenus tam āgāc ca svayaṃ cāpi dudoha tām
english: In olden days, it is said, Jamadagni resolved to perform a śrāddha; the cow of oblations came to him, and he himself milked her.

sanskrit: tat kṣīraṃ sthāpayām āsa nave bhāṇḍe dṛḍhe śucau tac ca krodhaḥ svarūpeṇa piṭharaṃ paryavartayat
english: He set that milk in a new vessel, firm and clean; and Anger, in his own embodied shape, overturned the pot.

sanskrit: jijñāsus tam ṛṣiśreṣṭhaṃ kiṃ kuryād vipriye kṛte iti saṃcintya durmedhā dharṣayām āsa tat payaḥ
english: Wishing to test that best of sages—what would he do when an offense was given—that evil-minded one, so reflecting, defiled the milk.

sanskrit: tam ājñāya muniḥ krodhaṃ naivāsya cukupe tataḥ sa tu krodhas tam āhedaṃ prāñjalir mūrtimān sthitaḥ
english: But the sage, recognizing him as Anger, was not in the least angered at him; whereupon that Anger, taking embodied form and standing with joined palms, said this to him:

sanskrit: jito 'smīti bhṛguśreṣṭha bhṛgavo hy atiroṣaṇāḥ loke mithyāpravādo 'yaṃ yat tvayāsmi parājitaḥ
english: "I am conquered, O best of the Bhṛgus! It is a false report in the world that the Bhṛgus are exceedingly prone to wrath, for I have been vanquished by you."

sanskrit: so 'haṃ tvayi sthito hy adya kṣamāvati mahātmani bibhemi tapasaḥ sādho prasādaṃ kuru me vibho
english: "Now today I stand at your mercy, who are forbearing and great of soul; I dread your austerity, O virtuous one. Show me your grace, O mighty lord."

sanskrit: janamejaya uvāca sākṣād dṛṣṭo 'si me krodha gaccha tvaṃ vigatajvaraḥ na mamāpakṛtaṃ te 'dya na manyur vidyate mama
english: Jamadagni said: "You have been seen by me face to face, O Anger. Go, with your fever gone. You have done me no wrong this day, and there is no resentment in me."

sanskrit: yān uddiśya tu saṃkalpaḥ payaso 'sya kṛto mayā pitaras te mahābhāgās tebhyo budhyasva gamyatām
english: "But those for whose sake this resolve concerning the milk was made by me—they are your forefathers, the greatly blessed; turn to them for understanding, and let you go."

sanskrit: ity ukto jātasaṃtrāsaḥ sa tatrāntaradhīyata pitṝṇām abhiṣaṅgāt tu nakulatvam upāgataḥ
english: Thus addressed, struck with terror, he vanished there; and through the curse-like contact of the forefathers he attained the state of a mongoose.

sanskrit: sa tān prasādayām āsa śāpasyānto bhaved iti taiś cāpy ukto yadā dharmaṃ kṣepsyase mokṣyase tadā
english: He propitiated them, that there might be an end to the curse; and he was told by them: "When you shall revile Dharma, then you shall be released."

sanskrit: taiś cokto yajñiyān deśān dharmāraṇyāni caiva ha jugupsan paridhāvan sa yajñaṃ taṃ samupāsadat
english: So bidden by them, scorning the regions sacred to sacrifice and the forests of righteousness, ranging about, he came at last to that sacrifice.

sanskrit: dharmaputram athākṣipya saktuprasthena tena saḥ muktaḥ śāpāt tataḥ krodho dharmo hy āsīd yudhiṣṭhiraḥ
english: Then, having reviled the son of Dharma over that measure of barley-meal, he, that Anger, was freed from the curse; for Dharma himself was Yudhiṣṭhira.

sanskrit: evam etat tadā vṛttaṃ tasya yajñe mahātmanaḥ paśyatāṃ cāpi nas tatra nakulo 'ntarhitas tadā
english: Thus did this come to pass at the sacrifice of that great-souled one; and there, even as we looked on, the mongoose vanished away.
